newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ministers agree to set up health monitoring network.
newsitem.headline: Ministers agree to set up health monitoring network.

text.p: European Union health ministers agreed unanimously on Thursday, despite Commission objections, to set up a network to monitor contagious diseases, EU officials said.
The political agreement was based on a Dutch Presidency compromise between the desire of member states to retain national control in a sensitive sector and the need to protect public health.
The European Commission says that the compromise waters down its proposals, preventing the EU from safeguarding the public against the spread of AIDS, rabies and other deadly diseases.

In 1996, the Commission proposed a compulsory system for sharing data on communicable diseases, notification and surveillance of selected diseases, consultation between member states on protective measures, especially at ports and airports.

But after some member states, notably Britain and Belgium, strongly resisted attempts to harmonise national rules, the Dutch Presidency suggested that it should be left to member states to decide how much information they would share.

The legal text of the political agreement will now be formally adopted without discussion as an "A" point at a future ministerial meeting and then sent to the European Parliament for a second reading under the co-decision procedure.
